agree.reason: A reader who left over price and is happy with the savings might try the $99 visit, but nothing makes the ongoing $25 extra a visit feel worth it, and the email never says 'no contract, cancel any time', which would have made the trial an easy yes.

honest.reason: Every figure matches the brief, and the email promises a regular cleaner and a named backup for sick days and holidays instead of the false 'same cleaner every single time'.

works_the_facts.reason: The email repeats the raw figures but derives almost nothing from them: it never notes that $99 is $41 under the app price, never turns 7 of 18 versus 1 of 18 into a clear turnover rate, and never frames the $25 gap in a more favourable way.

right_comparison.reason: It compares the app services fairly on price ($140) and on uninsured contractors, and shows the drop in cleaner turnover since July, though it doesn't say what an uninsured visit could cost the customer.

qualification.reason: The offer has a checkable end date (December 31), and the backup is tied to named cases (sick days and holidays), so the limit on the cleaner promise is concrete and honest.

objections.reason: It explains why the price is higher, but it doesn't spell out what insurance protects the customer from, and it leaves out the no-contract commitment that would answer this reader's fear of losing the savings.

fit.reason: It's a plain email of about 170 words, close to the 150 asked for, and it makes the regular-cleaner promise as strongly as the facts allow, with clear booking steps.
